challenge.method: Compared the pinned tag target and detail with the modern and legacy W3C paths, OSI link, separate document-license route, publisher title and the three uses of dates.
challenge.results: The legacy software URL and modern versioned route differ literally. Both records describe removal of the ownership notice and the ambiguous grant of 'use' and give the same activation date. The standalone document-license route lacks that identification in the inspected evidence. The OSI URL is a secondary pointer for this purpose. The December 13 release comment and December 31 label and activation cannot establish a single publication date.

limitations: SPDX reports release on December 13. W3C reports activation on December 31. An exact publication timestamp and historical redirect chain remain unverified. The record establishes neither byte equality nor project-specific applicability.
reasoning: At the tagged data commit, SPDX assigns the unnumbered identifier W3C to its December 31, 2002 edition label. Its historical W3C software URL, grant and distinctive change note identify the edition presented at W3C’s versioned software-license route. SCES §§6–7 require preservation of differing date assertions and attribution of external-index facts to an exact owner and revision. The correspondence survives those checks without resolving first publication.
